claims.text: The proposed intervention is incorporation of 2–4 at% silicon into a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Adding 2–4 at% silicon will enable in situ formation of a continuous SiO2 scale on the alloy surface.
The SiO2 scale formed by silicon addition will be adherent to the alloy substrate.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys in the target class form non-protective oxide scales at 1100°C.
Silicon promotes selective oxidation and development of a stable, slow-growing silica scale.
A continuous SiO2 layer acts as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
Reduced oxygen ingress lowers oxidation and subsequent degradation rates.
Adherence of the in situ silica scale limits spallation and fast oxygen-diffusion pathways.
The silicon-modified alloy will oxidize more slowly than the untreated alloy under identical conditions.
The silicon-modified alloy will form a thinner oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The silicon-modified alloy will form a more adherent oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The silicon-modified alloy will have improved resistance to oxygen-induced degradation relative to the untreated alloy.
Untreated alloys experience rapid growth and spallation of non-protective oxide scales at 1100°C in oxygen-rich environments over approximately 100 hours.
The hypothesized benefit is expected at approximately 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for exposure durations on the order of 100 hours.
The benefit may not extend to significantly lower temperatures or drastically different atmospheres.
